alternate_names: Dargah Hazrath Haji Ratan Hindi RA

history.dynasty: None (saint's tomb); the tomb structure is dated to the 13th century by historian Subhash Parihar, with repairs by Hindu and Muslim officials of the region in subsequent centuries
history.period: Saint died 1234-35 AD per some Islamic chronicles; tomb structure 13th century
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed: this is a MUSLIM dargah (the tomb of the Sufi saint Baba Haji Rattan, venerated jointly by Hindus, Muslims and Sikhs), not a Hindu temple. CORRECTION OF THE BRIEF'S LEGEND: the 'Hindu fakir / camel herder' version is garbled. The documented legends are multiple and contested: (1) Islamic accounts (e.g. narrators quoted on Wanderlog) say Haji Rattan was from a non-Muslim family of Bathinda, a TRADER in spices who travelled to Arabia, met the Prophet Muhammad in his youth, performed Haj (hence 'Haji'), was gifted a camel by the Prophet - and the tomb of that camel still stands near the shrine - and was granted a life of ~700 years; (2) other accounts (cited by scholar Himanshu Damle from H.A. Rose's Glossary of Tribes and Castes of the Punjab) ascribe him a NATH identity - a disciple of Gorakhnath, son of Raja Mankiya Parikshak; (3) he is recorded by medieval chroniclers including Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, and debated by al-Dhahabi (who rejected the long-life claim in his treatise Kasr Wathan Ratan). The Sikh connection is strong: Guru Nanak is said to have visited during his first udasi (the faqir threw a stone at him, which he caught and threw back; the faqir sought forgiveness); Guru Gobind Singh halted at the mausoleum on his way to Bathinda; a Gurdwara named Haji Rattan stands near the dargah. The present complex in Haji Rattan Nagar near Sabzi Mandi, Bathinda comprises the tomb (protected by an iron railing), a small mosque, a hujra and recent structures; the tomb of Pir Shah Chand lies outside the enclosure. Notably, the dargah, the Haji Rattan Gurdwara and a mosque share a common wall and have coexisted in harmony (per a Maps of India travel account), and the complex has a 'dhuna mubarak' room portraying both a Hindu trident and the Islamic panjatan pak - an icon of the Nath-Sufi-Bhakti encounter of medieval Punjab. A large pre-partition fair at the dargah is remembered in a poem of Babu Rajab Ali (1894-1979). The shrine is managed by the Punjab Wakf Board.

name: Peer Haji Rattan Dargah
town: Bathinda (CSV town correct - the dargah is in Haji Rattan Nagar near Sabzi Mandi, Bathinda)
town_description: Bathinda is an ancient Malwa-region city of Punjab (population ~2.85 lakh, 2011), known for the Qila Mubarak fort (where Razia Sultan was imprisoned in 1240), its history of visitations by the Sikh Gurus, and as one of North India's largest rail junctions. The Haji Rattan complex sits ~2 km outside the old city centre.
tradition: Islam (Sufi dargah, with joint Hindu-Muslim-Sikh veneration)

travel.airport: Bathinda Airport (BUP) has limited commercial service; Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar (~190 km) is the nearest major airport.
travel.railway: Bathinda Junction - one of North India's largest rail junctions; Haji Rattan Nagar / Sabzi Mandi area is in the city, a short auto-rickshaw ride away.
travel.road: The dargah complex is on Haji Rattan Road near Sabzi Mandi in Bathinda city, reachable by auto-rickshaw or e-rickshaw from the railway station.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (Punjab plains are extremely hot April-June).
